Sailing a boat

The Small sailing boat floats on any water in the game. You launch it from the hotbar, steer it from the helm and set the sails to catch the wind. Boats are not available on multiplayer servers yet.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 6 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides
Contents
  1. Launch a boat
  2. Pack up a boat
  3. Take the helm and sail
  4. Wind and tacking
  5. Boats and saving
  6. How this was checked

Launch a boat

Craft the Small sailing boat from the Timber recipes. Crafting it selects it, ready to launch. In Creative, take it from the catalog. The boat floats on any water: sea, lakes and all six water types, at their real surface height. Launching and packing up a sailing boat

Timber 1 recipes
RecipeMakesNeeds
Small sailing boat1 Small sailing boat
  • 32× Boards of any species (mixable)
  • 12× Plant fiber or Wool (mixable)
  • 8× Reeds

Crafting selects the boat ready to launch; it weighs 18 kg.

  1. Select the Small sailing boat in your hotbar or inventory.
  2. Look at open water within 6 m and right-click. The boat appears on the water, facing the way you look.
  3. In Survival, the launch uses one boat item. In Creative, no item is used.
Careful. The launch needs water under the whole hull, no blocks in the way of the hull or mast, and space clear of other boats. If it fails, the game says "Boat needs clear water and room for its hull and mast (8 boats maximum)" and nothing is used. You can have up to 8 boats in the world at once.

Pack up a boat

Packing a boat puts it back into your pack, so you can carry it to another lake or sea. Launching and packing up a sailing boat

  1. Walk up to a boat that has nobody at the helm and look at it from within 6 m.
  2. Hold Shift and right-click. You can hold any item.
  3. The game says Sailing boat packed, and a Small sailing boat item goes into your pack, in Survival and in Creative.
  • You need 18 capacity of free pack room. Otherwise the game says "Free 18 capacity to pack the boat".
  • A boat with 0 HP (wrecked) cannot be boarded or packed. Wrecks are not saved, and the game clears them the next time you launch a boat.
Good to know. Boats are not available on multiplayer servers yet. Launching or packing says "Boats aren't available on servers yet", and V says "Vehicles aren't available on servers yet".

Take the helm and sail

You can walk and jump on the wooden deck like normal ground. The helm is where you steer and set the sails. Within 9 m of a boat, the hint by the crosshair reads PRESS V TO ENTER SMALL SAILING BOAT. Sailing: deck, helm, sails, steering and camera

Key or actionWhat it does
VTake the helm, or step back to the cockpit. You must be within 9 m of the hull or on its deck.
W (hold)Raise the sail setting. The sails follow over about 2 seconds.
S (hold)Reef the sails (lower the setting).
SpaceLower the sails completely.
A / DSteer left or right. The rudder eases in and recentres.
C or F5Switch between first-person and chase view.
Hold AltLook around freely. The view swings back when you let go.
  • There is no reverse. Lower the sails to slow down, and steer to turn.
  • The boat can turn slowly while it is stopped. It turns faster the faster it sails.
  • The boat stops dead if its hull would run aground or hit another boat. It can only turn where the new heading still has water under the whole hull. If the boat is stuck on the shore, pack it up and launch it again.
  • Stepping off the helm stops the boat at once, and the sails lower by themselves. A boat with nobody at the helm does not drift.
  • At the helm, E does not open your pack and map travel is refused. Press V to step off first.

Wind and tacking

Each world has one wind direction, and it never changes. The wind strength depends on the weather: about 2.8 m/s in clear weather and up to 8.5 m/s in a thunderstorm. Seasons do not change the wind. Sailing: wind, speed and tacking

  • Running with the wind (sailing straight downwind) is fastest. The boat reaches the wind speed, up to its top speed of 6 m/s.
  • Sailing across the wind gives about two-thirds of the wind speed.
  • Within 45 degrees of sailing straight into the wind, the sails give no push. To go upwind, zig-zag: sail one side of the wind, then turn across it to the other side. This is called tacking.
  • Lower sails give less speed. Half sail gives half the speed.

Read the flags and the panel

  • The red pennant at the top of the mast points downwind, the way the air travels.
  • At the helm, a panel titled SAILBOAT sits at the top left, under the status line. Its flag box shows the same wind with the bow of your boat at the top.
  • WIND n M/S TO n gives the wind speed and the compass bearing the air blows towards: 0 is north, 90 east, 180 south and 270 west.
  • The panel says TACK: TURN ACROSS WIND when your bow is in the no-push zone, and BOW UP FLAG otherwise.
  • The line above shows the boat's HP, its speed in knots (KN), the sail setting (TRIM) and your compass heading (HDG).

Boats and saving

Up to 8 launched boats are saved with the world, with their position, heading and health. Your boats are still there when you load the world. Boats and saving

Tip. If you save while at the helm, you reload standing in the stopped boat's cockpit, not at the helm. Press V to take the helm again.
